page: Amazon Web Services r3.4xlarge is a legacy memory-optimized virtual machine delivered via the Xen hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor built on the x86_64 architecture operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. Its compute resource profile includes 8 physical cores presenting 16 dedicated vCPUs across two threads per core, backed by 25 MB of shared L3 cache and AVX instruction support. Memory capacity totals 122 GB, allocating 7.62 GB of system memory per vCPU. Storage is addressed via 320 GB of bundled local SSD space, while networking is configured with a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth profile. Accelerated GPU hardware is not present on this instance type.

Benchmark evaluation highlights the architectural characteristics of this previous-generation hardware. Multi-core compute capabilities sit within median ranges, as evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 14,028.83, a multi-core Geekbench score of 4,727.0, and an average stress-ng multi-threaded result of 13,890.81. Conversely, single-thread performance trails modern cloud standards, reflected by a Geekbench single-core score of 719.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1,322.59. Memory subsystem throughput remains solid, sustaining 88.29 GB/s on large uncached read blocks and 46.15 GB/s on uncached write blocks. Compression and decompression tests, including single-threaded gzip and multi-threaded bzip3, demonstrate lower throughput due to older microarchitecture limitations and the absence of advanced vector acceleration such as AVX-512.

From an efficiency perspective, the r3.4xlarge provides a high density of RAM per compute unit alongside bundled low-latency local storage. However, its older processor generation means compute throughput per resource allocation is lower than modern alternatives. It is unsuited for compute-heavy applications or modern deep learning pipelines. Instead, the instance is appropriate for memory-intensive workloads that prioritize RAM capacity and local storage over per-core processor speed, such as distributed memory caches, relational database systems, search index nodes, and batch extract-transform-load data pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r3.4xlarge is a third-generation memory-optimized instance running on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor running at 2.5 GHz, providing 8 physical cores and 16 dedicated vCPUs with 25 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is 122 GB, yielding 7.62 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance includes 320 GB of integrated local SSD storage, 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and does not include a GPU. Benchmark testing shows average multi-core processing performance alongside moderate memory bandwidth, reaching 88.29 GB/s uncached read throughput. Single-threaded performance and compression throughput are comparatively weak due to the legacy CPU microarchitecture lacking newer instruction set extensions like AVX-512. Given its generous memory footprint and bundled local SSD storage, the instance fits in-memory caching layers such as Redis, relational databases, and batch ETL jobs requiring large memory buffers over top-tier compute velocity.
